df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')
df['date'] = pd.to_datetime(df['date'], format='%m/%d/%y')
a = df[df.account_id=='S5Tfd67'].copy()

    mean=s.mean(); std=s.std()
    z=(s[anom_day]-mean)/std if std>0 else 0
    # robust: compare to median of other days
    med=s.median()
    if abs(z)>2.5 and s[anom_day]>med:
        print(f"{col}: anom={s[anom_day]:.2f} mean={mean:.2f} med={med:.2f} z={z:.2f}")

# Also check num_instances per instance_family on anomaly day vs distribution
inst = a.pivot_table(index='date', columns='instance_family', values='num_instances', aggfunc='sum').fillna(0)
row_a = inst.loc[anom_day]
q95 = inst.quantile(0.95); mx = inst.max()
out = row_a[(row_a > q95*1.3) & (row_a>=mx*0.9)]
print("instance counts at/near max on anomaly day:")
print(pd.DataFrame({'anom':out,'max':mx[out.index],'q95':q95[out.index],'median':inst.median()[out.index]}).to_string())
